subinhibitory antibiotic concentrations of tobramycin and ciprofloxacin, at concentrations used clinically for the treatment of chronic P. aeruginosa infections in CF, significantly increased the adherence of the bacteria to CF and non-CF tracheal epithelia, but not to bronchial epithelial cells, and that the increased bacterial adherence to CF tracheal epithelium was associated with increased production of the virulence factor pyocyanin.

1) subinhibitory antibiotic concentrations can enhance the ability of P. aeruginosa to adhere to epithelial cells, and this effect is more pronounced on cells derived from CF patients, and 2) subinhibitiory antibiotics can also enhance the ability of the bacterium to form biofilms.
